Section 3

Branches and programmes

Nineteen programmes on four branches, grown from the family tree and meeting at the Convention. Each page says what the programme is, what it needs, and how far the platform has got.

9 plan only6 built3 designed1 retired

Two ways of moving

People move in two directions, and they are kept apart (D39).

  • Along a branch, between programmes. How that works depends on the branch's shape. Education is a ladder by age, Leadership a ladder by capacity, Heritage a cluster with no "next", and Care a set of destinations.
  • Up the rungs inside one programme. Every programme uses the same five: hear, show up, take part, give or serve, lead (D25). Members never see a score, and moving down a rung is never a flag.

Pages marked Plan only have a register row and a written plan and little more. They say so, and where the record is silent they say that too.

Education · A ladder by age

From a teenager's first week at camp to a young adult's first leadership course. A person moves up by age, and a milestone opens an invitation to the next programme. The Arabic Program is the exception: it is open at any age. More about Education

Camp Ramallah

A residential summer camp bringing young members from across the US together for Ramallah heritage, Palestinian history and culture, outdoors. For most people it is the first rung of the whole federation.

Built Flagship Cohort
Arabic Program

Weekly virtual Arabic classes for adults, run with a Palestinian partner college: a conversational track in the Palestinian dialect and a traditional reading and writing track.

Plan only Cohort
Outstanding High School Senior Award

An award recognising community service and leadership in graduating high-school seniors. The register retired it in August 2026 by Board resolution, though afrp.org still offered it when the Hub's plans were written.

Retired Award
Scholarship

Financial support for college students of Ramallah descent: up to four years of undergraduate support, extended through graduation for medical students, with named scholarships alongside the general fund.

Built Flagship Award
Project Hope

A two-week, hands-on programme in Palestine that connects young adults to their ancestral homeland through volunteer service and meetings with local organisations, officials and youth.

Plan only Mission
Leadership Ramallah

A two-day summit for young Palestinian-American adults, held alongside the Mid-Year Meeting, with expert-led workshops on leadership, advocacy and cultural preservation.

Plan only Flagship Cohort

Leadership · A ladder by capacity

Service, advocacy and professional life. People enter at Emerging Leaders and move by what they are ready to take on, not by age. The order is a suggestion, never a prerequisite. More about Leadership

Emerging Leaders Summit

The entry rung of the Leadership branch. afrp.org has no page for it, and the record states nothing beyond its age band and its place on the branch.

Plan only other
Ramallah Business & Professional Network

A network for members in business and the professions: training courses, mentoring, networking events and a mixer at the Convention. It holds one voting seat on the AFRP Board.

Built Flagship other
Congressional Outreach

Year-round advocacy for Palestinian rights at every level of government and across party lines: members meet their own elected officials, and the committee briefs State Department and DHS officials.

Plan only Committee
Day of Action

A yearly advocacy summit on Capitol Hill: members meet their representatives and senators and attend advocacy-tools sessions with partner organisations.

Plan only other
Educational & Cultural Exchange Mission

Missions to Ramallah since 2015 for American journalists, educators, clergy and political leaders, plus graduate-student delegations, fellowships and cultural programming.

Plan only Cohort

Heritage · A cluster, used for life

The Ramallah Family Tree, the Preservation Project, Hathihe Ramallah and the Bookstore. There is no "next" here and no milestone invitations: people come and go all their lives, and nobody graduates from the archive to the magazine. The tree also holds every member's node, so the other branches draw on it too (D30, D53). More about Heritage

Ramallah Family Tree

The genealogy of the original Ramallah clans and their descendants, more than 30,000 people. It sits on the Heritage branch (D53). Every member still has a node on it, and a node is never a lineage claim (D30).

Built other
Ramallah Preservation Project

A digital archive of Ramallah's history, begun in 2020: photographs, documents, articles and oral histories with migrants and first-generation Americans, shown at convention exhibits and with a museum partner.

Plan only other
Hathihe Ramallah

The Federation's magazine since 1952, in English and Arabic, carrying family news, recognition lists and statutory notices. On the platform its printed sections are generated from live data at a copy freeze.

Built other
Bookstore

An online store for books, magazine back issues, clan books, merchandise and digital downloads, with member pricing for members in good standing.

Built other

Care · Destinations

The Medical Mission, Women to Women and Senior Living, with the Ramallah Foundation and the Endowed Fund shown as funds that people give to and cannot join. People arrive by choice or by capacity to give, never by progression. More about Care

Medical Mission

Volunteer physicians, specialists and health professionals from the US and Palestine building long-term health capacity in Palestine: prosthetics, eye and cancer screening, hospital equipment and workforce training.

Designed Flagship Mission
Women to Women

Direct financial help to women in Ramallah and their families for basic needs and self-improvement. Projects are proposed in writing from Ramallah and approved by a committee.

Plan only Committee
Senior Living Project

A capital project for a new senior residence in Ramallah, replacing a 1970s facility: about 30,000 square feet for 50 or more residents. Ground was broken in October 2023 and the cornerstone laid in June 2024.

Designed Campaign

The Convention · The junction where the branches meet

Once a year every branch meets at the Convention: the governance floor, programme gatherings and the community. It belongs to no branch and is a rung on none. More about The Convention

The Annual Convention

The Federation's annual gathering, held since 1959: governance, the election and the Assembly floor, the banquet, youth events and every programme's moment. It sits on no branch and is reachable from all of them.

Designed Flagship other

What is real here. By-law citations, decisions and the Federation's own strategy documents are real. People, households and money shown in the prototype and its fixture are fictional. No living person is named on these pages (D50).

Generated from davidsaah/afrp-strategy. Precedence (D41): the by-law texts, then the Decisions Register and design documents, then the prototype, then the Hub's code. Where the record is silent, these pages say so.
